amendments.stage: after preliminary scoring and before the final clean-commit run
changes: Use paired contrastive cases rather than claiming every pair is a minimal textual edit.
Report direct warmed judge-call latency and hook-process/IPC probes as separate boundaries.
Treat the originally planned event-to-outcome, resource, and matched Codex-turn measurements as not evaluated; they support no paper claim.
amendments.reason: The synthetic harness can identify process and IPC boundaries but cannot validly infer user-visible Codex latency or production resource behavior.

amendments.stage: after preliminary local scoring and before the final clean-commit run
changes: Add one independently prompted open-model judge baseline (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507) using deterministic decoding and the same strict output parser.
amendments.reason: User-provided ALL-partition GPU capacity made a reproducible larger-model calibration baseline feasible.

research_questions.rq1: How reliably do local compiled rules classify controlled, paired-contrast coding-agent events?
research_questions.rq2: What direct-judge latency and ingress reliability behavior can be established at explicitly instrumented local boundaries?
research_questions.rq3: Does RAP preserve the exact managed-rule input and revision provenance needed for a deterministic inspect-and-refine workflow?

primary_metric: mean across rules of positive-class F1
exclusions: inputs exceeding the rule byte limit
exact copies of examples embedded in the frozen specification
any native event not manually approved for release

claim_gates.timely: warm p95 event-to-outcome latency <= 3.0 seconds (not evaluated; no claim)
claim_gates.low_handoff_overhead: p95 hook handoff <= 0.250 seconds (not met in the preliminary process-boundary probe; no claim)
